Q1_forecast_level_vs_error.verbatim_quote: "CONSENSUS_EARNINGS_FORECAST is defined as the standardized mean 1-quarter ahead earnings per share forecast." (Table 1 notes, p. 3198) The paper consistently uses 'forecast' (level language) rather than 'forecast error', 'surprise', or 'unexpected earnings'. It is introduced as a control thus: "As an additional control for first-moment effects of Brexit, we add 1-quarter-ahead consensus earnings forecasts to our model." (Section IV.C.3, p. 3197). The phrase 'first-moment' in the paper's framework refers to the expected level (the mean of the cash-flow distribution), in contrast to 'second-moment' uncertainty effects — see e.g. p. 3195: "That same earnings forecasts evidence points to the Brexit vote having a 'second-moment' effect in terms of increased uncertainty regarding U.K.-exposed firms' expectations in 2016:Q1–Q2. In particular, EPS forecast dispersion of HIGH_UK_EXPOSURE firms increases significantly in early 2016." The paper never explicitly contrasts 'forecast level' versus 'forecast surprise/error', and never uses words such as 'surprise', 'unexpected earnings', 'actual minus forecast', or 'SUE'. The language strongly implies the LEVEL of the consensus forecast, but this is not stated verbatim as a level-vs-surprise disambiguation.
Q1_forecast_level_vs_error.source_location: Table 1 notes, p. 3198; Section IV.C.3, p. 3197; Figure 4 discussion, p. 3195

Q2_standardized_denominator.verbatim_quote: "CONSENSUS_EARNINGS_FORECAST is defined as the standardized mean 1-quarter ahead earnings per share forecast." This is the entire construction statement. The paper does NOT specify what 'standardized' means. There is no statement that the EPS forecast is scaled by share price, by total assets, by analyst forecast dispersion (STDEV), or by any other denominator. There is no statement that it is z-scored cross-sectionally within calendar quarter, or normalized over the panel. The Figure 4 discussion (p. 3195) mentions: "Beginning in 2015:Q1, we obtain the 1-year-ahead earnings per share (EPS) forecasts for each firm in our sample and compute the mean and standard deviation of forecasts. We quantify earnings forecast uncertainty for firms in the high and low βUK_i groups by constructing 1.5-standard-deviation intervals around their group mean forecasts in Figure 4." — but this is for the figure visualization (and uses 1-year-ahead, not 1-quarter-ahead) and does NOT describe the construction of the regression control variable. The Supplementary Material (Table C3 notes) refers to "1-quarter-ahead CONSENSUS_EARNINGS_FORECASTS" as an input to propensity-score matching but provides no construction detail.
Q2_standardized_denominator.source_location: Table 1 notes, p. 3198; Section IV.C.2 / Figure 4, p. 3195; Supplementary Tables C2, C3, C7

Q3_ibes_data_fields.verbatim_quote: "Analyst forecast data are obtained from I/B/E/S." (Section IV.B, p. 3193) This is the only I/B/E/S-related statement in the paper. The paper does NOT mention any specific I/B/E/S data field, file, or filter: it names no MEASURE (EPS vs. SAL vs. CPS), no FISCALP / FPI value (1-quarter vs. 1-year), no estimate statistic (MEAN, MEDEST, STDEV), no ACTUAL field, no detail file vs. summary file, and no STATPERS / FPEDATS / ANNDATS variable. No I/B/E/S documentation references appear in main text, Table 1 notes, Section IV.B–C, equation (14) discussion, or any of Supplementary Appendices A–E.

Q4_merge_methodology.verbatim_quote: The paper does NOT describe the I/B/E/S–Compustat merge methodology. It states only: "Analyst forecast data are obtained from I/B/E/S" (Section IV.B, p. 3193). No mention is made of merging by TICKER, CUSIP, IBES TICKER, CIK, PERMNO, or GVKEY. No mention is made of which I/B/E/S date field (STATPERS, FPEDATS, ANNDATS, REVDATS, ACTDATS) is aligned to which Compustat date field (DATADATE, RDQ, FYEARQ + FQTR). No statement specifies whether the match is within the same calendar quarter, with a lead/lag, before/after the earnings announcement, or rolled forward. Supplementary Table C1's final filter step — "Drop if missing CRSP and I/B/E/S controls — 41,630" — confirms an I/B/E/S link is required for the regression sample but provides no merge details.
Q4_merge_methodology.source_location: Section IV.B, p. 3193; Supplementary Table C1

Q5_timing_of_1_quarter_ahead.verbatim_quote: The paper consistently uses the phrase '1-quarter-ahead' but never spells out the precise time alignment. Relevant verbatim statements: (a) Table 1 notes: "CONSENSUS_EARNINGS_FORECAST is defined as the standardized mean 1-quarter ahead earnings per share forecast." (p. 3198) (b) Section IV.C.3 (immediately after the eq. 14 CONTROLS_{i,t-1} statement): "As an additional control for first-moment effects of Brexit, we add 1-quarter-ahead consensus earnings forecasts to our model." (p. 3197) (c) Supplementary Tables C2 and C3 also refer to "1-quarter-ahead CONSENSUS_EARNINGS_FORECAST". Crucially, the paper lists this variable separately from the explicitly lagged controls: in Section IV.C.3 (p. 3197), the lagged firm-level controls are enumerated as "lagged stock returns, Tobin's Q, cash flow, logged assets, and sales growth" — CONSENSUS_EARNINGS_FORECAST is introduced AFTER this list with the distinct phrasing "As an additional control...we add 1-quarter-ahead consensus earnings forecasts", suggesting the forecast is forward-looking (for quarter t+1) attached to observation t, rather than lagged. However, this is not stated verbatim and the exact (forecast-vintage-date, target-quarter) tuple is not specified.
Q5_timing_of_1_quarter_ahead.source_location: Table 1 notes, p. 3198; Section IV.C.3, p. 3197; equation (14) and surrounding text, pp. 3196–3197

Q6_missing_value_and_coverage.verbatim_quote: The paper does NOT explain the lower N for CONSENSUS_EARNINGS_FORECAST in Table 1 Panel A (N=42,031 vs. ~67K–78K for other variables). The relevant filter language is in Supplementary Table C1: "Drop if missing CRSP and I/B/E/S controls — 41,630". No discussion of I/B/E/S coverage limitations, of which firms tend to be missing from I/B/E/S, or of any CONSENSUS_EARNINGS_FORECAST-specific filter beyond the global "Drop if missing CRSP and I/B/E/S controls" step appears anywhere in the main text, table notes, or supplementary appendices A–E. Note: the Panel A N of 42,031 is only ~400 observations above the final regression sample size of 41,630, which the paper does not flag or interpret.
Q6_missing_value_and_coverage.source_location: Supplementary Table C1; Table 1 Panel A, p. 3198

Q7_corrigendum_corrections.verbatim_quote: Corrigendum, in full (p. 3313): "In the original publication of this article, appendices A and B were missing. The original article, and the supplementary material, have since been updated." The corrigendum addresses ONLY the omission of theoretical Appendices A (Model Analysis and Results) and B (Proofs) from the supplementary material. It documents NO correction to CONSENSUS_EARNINGS_FORECAST — neither its definition, its summary statistics, its construction, its I/B/E/S source, its standardization, its timing, nor its role in the regression specification.

summary_note: Six of seven sub-questions resolve to 'not_specified_in_paper' or 'partially_specified'. The paper's complete description of CONSENSUS_EARNINGS_FORECAST consists of: (i) one definitional sentence in Table 1 notes ('standardized mean 1-quarter ahead earnings per share forecast'); (ii) one sourcing sentence in Section IV.B ('Analyst forecast data are obtained from I/B/E/S'); (iii) one role-of-control sentence in Section IV.C.3 ('additional control for first-moment effects of Brexit'). The paper does NOT pin down: the meaning of 'standardized' (price-scaled, asset-scaled, dispersion-scaled, or z-scored), the specific I/B/E/S fields used, the merge methodology, or the exact date alignment of '1-quarter-ahead'. The corrigendum makes no corrections to this variable. Note the SD of 3.51 reported in Table 1 Panel A is large in absolute terms — far too large to be a price-scaled EPS forecast in normal units, and inconsistent with a pure z-score (which would have SD≈1). This is unexplained by the paper. Most plausible (but unstated) interpretation: dispersion-scaled forecast (EPS / forecast STDEV) or analyst-coverage-standardized.
